title: Integers, Opposites and Absolute Value
seo_title: Grade 7 Integers and Absolute Value Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 7)
standard_text: Describe the set of integers; use positive and negative numbers to describe directions or opposites in real-life situations; locate integers on the number line; compare and order integers; identify the absolute value of an integer, and its meaning on the number line.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 integers worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: integers in real life, the number line, opposites, comparing and ordering, and absolute value. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Numbers increase to the right on a number line.
key_sub: |a| is the distance from 0: never negative.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The integers are …, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, … Positive and negative numbers describe opposites: above or below sea level, gain or loss, deposit or withdrawal.
  • On a number line, numbers increase to the right. −3 > −8.
  • Opposites are the same distance from 0 on different sides: 5 and −5.
  • The absolute value |a| is the distance from 0, so it is never negative: |−7| = 7.

Examples

Example

Order −4, 2, −9, 0

farthest left first

Answer: −9, −4, 0, 2

Example

|−12|

12 units from 0

Answer: 12

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
−8 > −3−8 is farther left, so it is smaller.
Negative absolute value|−7| = 7.
Opposite or absolute value?The opposite of −7 is 7; the opposite of 7 is −7.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 7 ask about integers?
faq.a: Describe the set of integers, use positive and negative numbers for directions or opposites, locate integers on the number line, compare and order them, and identify the absolute value.
The distance of −4 from 0, which is 4.

items.q: In a hotel, the pool is 2 floors below ground level. The gym is 5 floors above ground level. Which number represents the floor of the pool?
items.e: “Below ground level” is the negative direction, so the number is −2. Here, 0 would mean ground level.

items.q: In a golf game, Trisha finished 3 strokes over par and Vincent finished 2 strokes under par. Which number represents Vincent’s score compared with par?
items.e: “Under par” is the negative direction, so the number is −2. Here, 0 would mean par.

items.q: A thermometer shows degrees Celsius (°C). What does 0°C mean?
c: the temperature at which water boils
the temperature at which water freezes
items.e: On the Celsius scale, water freezes at 0°C. Temperatures colder than that are negative, so 0°C is not the coldest possible: water freezes at 0°C.

items.q: In an elevator, floors below the ground floor are negative. What does floor 0 mean?
c: a floor that does not exist
items.e: Floors above ground are positive and floors below are negative. 0 is the level between them: the ground floor.

items.q: An object can have a positive or a negative electric charge. What does a charge of 0 mean?
c: it has a very large charge
items.e: Positive and negative charges balance out at 0. An object with a charge of 0 is neutral.

items.q: What is the opposite of 9?
items.e: The opposite is the same distance from 0, on the other side of 0. Change the sign: the opposite of 9 is −9. (Flipping the number to 19 gives the reciprocal, not the opposite.)

items.q: What is the opposite of −14?
items.e: The opposite is the same distance from 0, on the other side of 0. Change the sign: the opposite of −14 is 14. (Flipping the number to −114 gives the reciprocal, not the opposite.)

items.q: What is the opposite of 34?

items.e: The opposite is the same distance from 0, on the other side of 0. Change the sign: the opposite of −2.5 is 2.5. (Flipping the number to −0.4 gives the reciprocal, not the opposite.)

items.q: What is the opposite of 0?
items.e: The opposite of a number is the same distance from 0 on the other side. 0 is 0 units from itself, so the opposite of 0 is 0.

items.q: What is −(−7)?
items.e: −(−7) means “the opposite of −7.” −7 is 7 units to the left of 0, so its opposite is 7 units to the right: 7.

items.q: What is the opposite of the opposite of 11?
items.e: The opposite of 11 is −11. The opposite of that is 11 again. Taking the opposite twice brings you back: 11.

items.q: What is −(−2.5)?
items.e: −(−2.5) means “the opposite of −2.5.” −2.5 is 2.5 units to the left of 0, so its opposite is 2.5 units to the right: 2.5.

items.q: What is the opposite of the opposite of −6?
items.e: The opposite of −6 is 6. The opposite of that is −6 again. Taking the opposite twice brings you back: −6.

items.q: What is −(−(−4))?
items.e: Work from the inside: −(−4) = 4, and the opposite of 4 is −4. Three minus signs: −4.

items.q: Two numbers are opposites. On a number line, each one is 6 units from 0. What are the two numbers?
items.e: Opposites are the same distance from 0 on different sides. 6 units right of 0 is 6, and 6 units left is −6: 6 and −6. (3 and −3 are 6 units apart, but each is only 3 units from 0.)

items.q: Point A is 9 units to the left of 0. Point B is at the opposite of point A. Where is point B?
items.e: A is at −9. Its opposite is 9, the same distance from 0 on the other side: 9 units to the right of 0. (18 units is the distance from A to B, not from 0 to B.)

items.q: Which statement is true?
c: −8 and 8 are on the same side of 0
items.e: −(−8) means the opposite of −8, which is 8. −8 and 8 are on different sides of 0, each 8 units away. True: −(−8) = 8.

items.q: Which number is greater, −7 or −3? Why?
c: −7, because it is to the left of −3
−3, because it is to the left of −7
−3, because it is to the right of −7
items.e: −3 is to the right of −7 on the number line, so −3 > −7. Both are negative: the one farther from 0 (−7) is less. Being farther from 0 does not make a negative number greater.

items.q: Compare 0.5 and −1.5. Which statement is true?
items.e: 0.5 is to the right of −1.5 on the number line, so 0.5 > −1.5. A positive number is always greater than a negative number.

items.q: The statement −2 < 4 is true. What does it tell you about the number line?

items.e: “−2 < 4” means −2 is less than 4, so −2 is to the left of 4 on the number line.

items.q: Compare 0 and −6. Which statement is true?
items.e: 0 is to the right of −6 on the number line, so 0 > −6. Every negative number is less than 0.

items.q: What is |−8|?
items.e: Absolute value is the distance from 0. −8 is 8 units from 0, so |−8| = 8. An absolute value is never negative.

items.q: What is |15|?
items.e: 15 is positive and is 15 units from 0, so |15| = 15. The absolute value of a positive number is the number itself.

items.q: What is |−2.5|?
items.e: Absolute value is the distance from 0. −2.5 is 2.5 units from 0, so |−2.5| = 2.5. An absolute value is never negative.

items.q: Compare |−2.5| and |−6|. Which statement is true?
Which numbers have an absolute value of 2.5?
items.e: Both 2.5 and −2.5 are 2.5 units from 0, so |2.5| = 2.5 and |−2.5| = 2.5.

items.q: How far is 9 from 0 on the number line?
items.e: Count the spaces from 0 to 9, not the tick marks: 9 units. Distance is never negative, so |9| = 9.

items.q: Compare |−7| and |7|. Which statement is true?
items.e: |−7| = 7 and |7| = 7. Opposites are the same distance from 0, so |−7| = |7|.

items.q: How far is −6 from 0 on the number line?
items.e: Count the spaces from 0 to −6, not the tick marks: 6 units. Distance is never negative, so |−6| = 6.

items.q: What is |−34|?
items.e: Absolute value is the distance from 0. −34 is 34 unit from 0, so |−34| = 34. An absolute value is never negative.

items.q: What is |−24|?
items.e: Absolute value is the distance from 0. −24 is 24 units from 0, so |−24| = 24. An absolute value is never negative.

items.q: Which number is less than −5 but has an absolute value less than 9?
Look at −4 and −9. Which statement is false?
items.e: −4 is to the right of −9, so −4 > −9, not −4 < −9. The other statements are true: |−4| = 4 and |−9| = 9, so |−4| < |−9|.

items.q: Jenny says the number with the greater absolute value is always the greater number. Is she right?
c: Yes. It is true for every number.
items.e: It is not true for negative numbers. −8 is farther from 0 than 3, so |−8| > |3|. But −8 is to the left of 3, so −8 < 3.

items.q: Compare −9 and 4. Which statement is true?
items.e: Order: −9 is to the left of 4, so −9 < 4. Absolute value: |−9| = 9 and |4| = 4, so |−9| > |4|. The order and the absolute values do not point the same way.

items.q: Look at −7 and 2. Which statement is false?
items.e: −7 is to the left of 2, so −7 < 2, not −7 > 2. The other statements are true: |−7| = 7 and |2| = 2, so |−7| > |2|.

items.q: Compare −12 and −5. Which statement is true?
items.e: Order: −12 is to the left of −5, so −12 < −5. Absolute value: |−12| = 12 and |−5| = 5, so |−12| > |−5|. The order and the absolute values do not point the same way.

items.q: Which number is less than 3 but has a greater absolute value than 3?
items.e: Check both parts for each number. −4: −4 < 3, |−4| = 4; 4: 4 > 3, |4| = 4; 2: 2 < 3, |2| = 2; −2: −2 < 3, |−2| = 2. Only −4 fits both.

items.q: Compare −3 and −8. Which statement is true?
items.e: Order: −3 is to the right of −8, so −3 > −8. Absolute value: |−3| = 3 and |−8| = 8, so |−3| < |−8|. The order and the absolute values do not point the same way.

items.q: Maria says −10 > −2 because 10 > 2. Is she right?
c: No. −10 is to the left of −2, so −10 < −2.
items.e: 10 > 2 compares the absolute values: |−10| > |−2|. For the numbers themselves, −10 is to the left of −2, so −10 < −2.

items.q:
Order the numbers from least to greatest absolute value.
2,  −6,  −4.5,  1
items.e: Find each absolute value: |2| = 2, |−6| = 6, |−4.5| = 4.5, |1| = 1. Closest to 0 comes first: 1, 2, −4.5, −6. This is not the same as ordering the numbers (−6, −4.5, 1, 2).
